why: A real function start that no detection pass finds, so nothing in disasm/functions.json contains it and nothing contains the switch it dispatches. The bytes are unambiguous: 0x000A5B5E is a ret, 0x000A5B5F is a single alignment nop, and 0x000A5B60 is `sub esp,0x50; push ebx; push ebp; push esi; push edi; mov esi,ecx` -- a __thiscall prologue after a terminated function. It is missed because the only edge into it is a direct `jmp` from the one-instruction thunk sub_000A6100, so it is filed as a tail-jump alias of whatever body the sweep was already in rather than as a start of its own. Five overlapping aliases (0x000A59B0, 0x000A5A00, 0x000A5A70, 0x000A5AC0, 0x000A5AF0) then run through it and all end at 0x000A5B8C, the dispatching jump. THE COST, measured 19 Sep 2026: the function's switch at 0x000A5B85 reads the table at 0x000A60A4, whose five arms all sit past 0x000A5B8C, so lifter.py's _analyze_switch_table finds no arm inside [func_start, func_end), throws the table away, and emits RECOMP_ITAIL. None of the four non-default arms has a translated body, so the runtime lookup fails and RECOMP_ITAIL's unresolved path runs `g_esp += 4; g_eax = 0; return`. That is correct for a real tail jump, whose caller has already run its epilogue and left esp on the return address, and wrong here by the whole frame: 0x50 of locals plus four pushes, 0x60. The function returns 0x60 short with its epilogue unrun, and because ebx/esi/edi are globals in this ABI every caller above it then pops them from the wrong slots. That is the 19 Sep skating crash. The deficit was derived twice, independently and to the same number: 0x50+4*4 from this prologue, and 0x60 from the guest ESP in all four of the player's crash logs, where the walker's pre-corruption frame base is 0x0050FE5C and the observed ESPs are 0x0050FDFC minus a whole number of 0x18-byte walker frames. Seed the PROLOGUE, never an arm: an arm seeded as a start truncates its owner at the dispatching jump and is exactly how this class of defect is created. 0x000A5B60 is a genuine entry, so RECOMP_SEED_INTERIOR's demotion pass correctly keeps it -- measured, it survives with 1333 other interior seeds dropped around it.
